submission.name: Campus Cadence
submission.tagline: A compact ride display for campus couriers, with a weekly distance board.
submission.inspiration: We wanted to make a simple ride readout for students who bike between campus buildings to deliver club materials or help with events. A weekly distance board seemed like a fun way for small volunteer crews to compare how much ground they cover.
submission.what_it_does: The prototype reads location data to estimate a rider's speed and distance, then presents the ride on a small display. A companion website is meant to collect weekly totals for a crew leaderboard; the map view is a separate demonstration of the location data.
submission.how_we_built_it: We used an ESP32 with a GPS module and Arduino-style C++ code to calculate speed and mileage from successive positions. When the module struggled to get a fix, we also tried passing phone location data to the board. The display, website, and map each have working pieces, but ride data is not yet reliably connected to the leaderboard.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: The GPS receiver took a long time to lock onto satellites, so location and speed readings were inconsistent. We also designed the case before accounting for space for a battery and button, then had to modify the print by hand.
submission.accomplishments: We worked out the basic distance and speed calculations and built a compact display concept around them. We also made a first pass at a map and weekly comparison page, though those parts still need a dependable shared data flow.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned that GPS location quality changes a lot with the environment and that using a phone as a location source brings its own connection work. The hardware packaging also taught us to plan for the battery and controls before printing an enclosure.
submission.whats_next: Next we would improve GPS reception, connect each ride to the website automatically, and add a more personalized display. An optional gyroscope could estimate incline for riders who want more detail about their route.
